The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{2}=4,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1(x-(-1))(x-4)(x-(-2\text{i}))(x-(2\text{i})) \\  & =1(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}+x-4x-4)({x}^{2}+(2\text{i}-2\text{i})x-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-3x-4)({x}^{2}+4) & = \\ {x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3}-12x-4{x}^{2}-16 & = \\ {x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16.$

Question 6
?

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial f(x). Find f(x) given that the coefficient of the quartic term is 1.

a
x4+3x3−5x2+2x−8
b
x4+10x2−2x−16
c
x4−3x3+10x2−2x−8
d
x4−3x3−5x2+8
e
x4−3x3−12x−16
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the diagram, we see that f(x) has roots x1=−1, x2=4, and x3,4=±2i. Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is a=1. Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

f(x)=a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)(x−x4)=1(x−(−1))(x−4)(x−(−2i))(x−(2i))=1(x+1)(x−4)(x+2i)(x−2i)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(x+1)(x−4)(x+2i)(x−2i)=(x2+x−4x−4)(x2+(2i−2i)x−(2i)2)=(x2−3x−4)(x2+4)=x4+4x2−3x3−12x−4x2−16=x4−3x3−12x−16.

Therefore, f(x)=x4−3x3−12x−16.
